name: The Poplar of Park Wielkopolski

location.address: Park Wielkopolski (Zieleniec Wielkopolski), Ochota, roughly 85m from the parks published ash trees (war_026)

access: Free. Stands in Park Wielkopolski, the same historic public park (laid out 1938) as the already-published Ash Trees of Park Wielkopolski (war_026), open at all times.
transport: Ochota district, Park Wielkopolski, between ul. Filtrowa and ul. Leczycka; same stop as war_026
verify_notes: Third natural monument in Park Wielkopolski, alongside the two ashes already published as war_026 (whose own story already flags a poplar of unrecorded size somewhere in the park). GDOS/CRFOP register entry PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1465011.4749 is a single-object (jednoobiektowy) designation from 2019-09-26, giving a tree-level coordinate but no species beyond genus (Topola - Populus sp.), no girth and no height; pl.wikipedia's reproduction of the Warsaw register (fetched as wikitext) confirms the same designation date and gives no measurement either. Species is genuinely unclear even to the Commons photographer, whose own file description reads "Topola (niejasny gatunek)" (poplar, unclear species) -- publish as Populus sp. and ask the reader. Alive-evidence: five Commons photos (CC BY-SA 4.0, user Panek) taken 2019-11 and 2020-04/07, all captioned as this pomnik przyrody; no photo more recent than 2020 was found this pass and no news of removal either, so curation_status is flagged on recency rather than on doubt. Distance to war_026: roughly 85m, same park, same walk. Do NOT confuse with the OTHER two Warsaw poplar natural monuments already published/known: Topola Obrońców (=war_002, ul. Grojecka) and Topola Narutowicza (still a lead, ul. Parkowa) -- three different trees, same species, same city.

name: Starynkiewicz's Yew

location.address: Zespol Stacji Filtrow w Warszawie (Warsaw Water Filters), beside the pressure/water tower, ul. Koszykowa 81, Ochota

access: Restricted, honestly: stands inside the working MPWiK Warsaw Water Filters complex (Zespol Stacji Filtrow), which the public may enter only on scheduled, ticketed guided tours (summer Sunday and selected-weekday open days, plus occasional night tours), not as a free walk-in site. Confirmed via MPWiK's own current visiting-programme page (mpwik.com.pl) listing specific 2026 tour dates.
transport: Ochota district, ul. Koszykowa / ul. Raszynska; trams on Al. Niepodleglosci and Raszynska pass nearby
verify_notes: Named for Sokrat Starynkiewicz, the Russian-appointed President (mayor) of Warsaw 1875-1892 who initiated the modern Warsaw water and sewage system built 1883-1886 to William Lindley and William Heerlein Lindley's design; the tree stands on the very site he built, beside its pressure tower, and a bust of Starynkiewicz was unveiled near the same tower in 1907 (pl.wikipedia, cited to a 2003 monograph). GDOS/CRFOP register (kodinspire PL.ZIPOP.1393.PP.1465011.3313, designated 1975-10-30, jednoobiektowy/single-object with a tree-level coordinate) gives: multi-stemmed (wielopniowy) common yew, height 8m, six stem girths 56/51/73/43/48/38 cm (recorded girth_cm as the largest stem, 73cm; this is a stem count not a single trunk, say so if used). Second, independent source: pl.wikipedia's dedicated article Zespol Stacji Filtrow w Warszawie (fetched directly, not a search summary) states on its own page, citing bip.warszawa.pl, that the grounds hold two natural monuments, "a multi-stemmed common yew (called the Starynkiewicz Yew, by the water tower) and a common horse chestnut (on the Raszynska street side)" -- an independent account of the same tree, name, species and position. A third: a dated Commons photo (2017-07-08, CC BY-SA 3.0 pl, Adrian Grycuk) captioned with the same name and location. Alive-evidence is from 2017 (9 years old); no delisting or removal note found in the wikitext (unlike the nearby chestnut entry, which explicitly notes one of two trunks was delisted in 2012), and the site is a maintained heritage park with a 100+-year plane avenue, so flagged on recency rather than on doubt. The complex also holds a second, already-distinct natural monument (a chestnut) not investigated this pass, plus an avenue of centenarian London planes -- possible future leads in the same access-restricted site. NOT to be confused with the ordinary chestnut/ash pair already catalogued elsewhere in the register near Pulawska (different trees, different location).
